jobs.title: Mid-Market Customer Success Manager - Americas
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About this Role

Hi, I’m Denise, and I’m the Head of High-Touch (Mid-Market) Customer Success at Ashby. Our team is passionate about shaping and scaling an exceptional customer experience for our high-touch customer segment, which primarily supports mid-market and growth-stage organizations. I’m excited to be hiring our next CSM as we continue expanding globally.

As a member of our Customer Success team, you will help us continue to grow our High-Touch Customer Success function. In this role, you’ll partner closely with customers to drive adoption, deliver strategic guidance, conduct product trainings and partnership reviews, and identify opportunities for expanded use cases and long-term value realization. You’ll also collaborate with a talented group of CSMs across the High-Touch team to continuously evolve how we support companies ranging from high-growth startups to public enterprises.

Ashby is designed to be powerful and flexible, allowing customers to tailor the platform to their unique hiring processes and workflows. Because of this, there is a lot to learn. You will become both a product and domain expert, enabling customers to make the most of Ashby and drive hiring excellence across their organizations.

Role Requirements:

  • You have a strong track record of Customer Success experience in B2B SaaS (at least two years), supporting customers through the adoption and long-term optimization of complex technologies. You enjoy building trusted partnerships with customers and helping them realize measurable value throughout the customer lifecycle.

  • You have experience managing a portfolio of approximately 60 mid-market customers with over $1.5M in total ARR. You’re comfortable balancing proactive engagement across a broad book of business while building strong relationships with a diverse set of stakeholders to drive adoption, retention, and growth.

  • You have experience partnering cross-functionally with teams such as Sales, Marketing, Product, Support, and Operations to advocate for customer needs and deliver a seamless customer experience.

  • You enjoy becoming a product expert and have demonstrated this in previous Customer Success roles. You create “aha” moments by tailoring trainings, workflow guidance, and strategic recommendations to each customer’s unique goals and challenges.

  • You’ve worked with technically complex products and bring strong curiosity and problem-solving skills to understanding how systems, workflows, and integrations operate in practice

You Should Apply If:

  • 📣 You demonstrate mastery of clear communication. You ask questions with precision and can explain complex concepts in simple terms.

  • 🎧 You are a great listener. You see your role as providing the voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our product roadmap continues delivering value.

  • 📊You enjoy working with a larger book of varied customers, and can effectively prioritise your time to make the biggest impact.

  • 🧩 You’re energized by learning and supporting a complex product. You enjoy diving deep into technical details, navigating advanced configurations, and data workflows, and you enjoy helping customers make sense of them.

  • 🧑‍🏫 You love to teach. Whether it’s a complex report to a very tenured data analyst, or a workflow to a brand new recruiter, who is new to SaaS tools, you see every teaching moment as an opportunity.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You obsess over sending crisp follow-up emails, on time. You take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates.

  • ⚡️ You move fast. You leverage tools/technology to maximize your time. You are at home managing a wide range of customers, and prioritizing effectively.

  • 🗺️ You're energized by an ever-improving work environment. Our team is growing, and continually iterating on processes - we live by our Operating Principle of "Implement Continuous Improvement"

  • 📊 You are always looking for ways to improve your work through data.

Why you shouldn’t apply:

  • You thrive with a smaller, more focused book of customers,. Our Mid-Market CSMs typically manage a book of 60+ customers, balancing personalized relationships with efficient, scalable support.

  • You're interested in managing customer accounts with well-defined touchpoints (rather than excited by the fluidity required of early stage CS work)

  • You shine as an exclusively commercial CSM, motivated by variable compensation. While our team's north star metric is revenue retention, we focus on adoption and engagement as our leading indicators. For renewal negotiation and upsell, we have a lovely team of Contract Managers. As such, this role does not currently include variable pay.

  • You’re afraid of rolling up your sleeves. If the idea of getting in the weeds with a customer about the nuance between a time in process report and a time to hire report feels too granular, or project managing a workflow change for offer approvals feels “beneath you”, this job isn’t going to be for you.

About Ashby

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website: https://www.ashbyhq.com/

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough - we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

  • Intro Call with Ashby Recruiting - 30 Minutes

  • Hiring Manager Interview - 45 Minutes

  • Mock Customer Call - 45 Minutes

  • Final Round - 1 hour

    • Rather than a traditional panel interview with a large group, we structure our panel into two focused conversations. This gives you the opportunity to meet with multiple team members in a more conversational setting centered on specific topics, instead of a formal Q&A. You'll discuss how you approach problem solving, dive into a product complexity exercise, then wrap up with a quick closing call with the hiring manager.

Benefits

  • You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Integrations Consultant - Americas
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hi! I'm John, Ashby's Head of Professional Services. One of my favorite aspects of Ashby is our operating principle of Continuous Improvement. Coupled with our principle of caring deeply about our customers, we often find ourselves wondering ‘what is a better way to accomplish this’. That’s why I am thrilled to be hiring our next Integrations Consultant! As the third member of our Integrations Consulting team (within Ashby’s Customer Success organization), you’ll have the opportunity to lead customer facing engagements, focusing on complex technical projects for some of our most strategic customers.

About this role:

As our next Integrations Consultant, you’ll be responsible for defining, managing, and executing the technical requirements for strategic customers, specifically those implementing Ashby with one of our custom-built HCM integrations. You will work with customers with varying levels of integration sophistication advising on integration best practices, technical configurations, and working with a customer’s internal expert on how to best achieve their goals. You will use your existing knowledge of both integrations and the products we will be integrating with to consult with our customers, helping them get up and running swiftly with Ashby, so they can ultimately achieve their desired business outcomes. You will partner with Product/Engineering, Implementation Specialists, CSMs, Sales Engineers, and other cross functional partners to achieve this. Ideally, this hire would be located in the EST time zone.

Role requirements:

  • Enterprise Human Capital Management (HCM) Integration Experience: You have extensive experience managing and executing integrations with Workday, as well as other enterprise-grade HCM solutions like UKG, ADP, Oracle, and SAP SuccessFactors (defining the work, aligning with stakeholders, communicating the project plan, and ultimately delivering results in accordance with the agreed upon expectations). You keep the team on track to ensure milestones are met. We’d love it if you have a Workday HCM certification. Even better if you’ve also managed integrations with tools listed under Integrations on our Ashby Knowledge Base.

  • Customer Centricity: You are adept at understanding customer needs and tailoring implementations to meet their specific requirements. You build strong customer relationships by maintaining high levels of engagement and communication; you’re the customer’s proactive guide and advocate throughout the implementation period.

  • Change Management: You are experienced in navigating change management processes and helping customers adapt to new systems and a refreshed approach.

  • Technical Proficiency: You have a solid understanding of a complex product (ideally Ashby) and its technical intricacies; you are technically curious and creative.

  • Consultative: You take pride in advising customers on best practices specific to their usage of software to ensure optimal value.

  • Innovative & Principled: You proactively address thematic customer opportunities and improve our processes accordingly. You don’t rely on ‘I’ve seen this done’ but instead think critically to solve problems.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration: You effectively partner with cross-functional stakeholders across Customer Success, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Operations to align and define progress.

You could be a great fit if:

  • 📣 You demonstrate clear communication. You ask clarifying questions with precision and can distill complex concepts into simple themes.

  • ⚙️ People technology expertise: You have proven experience managing complex integrations with people technology like Workday or other ERPs, including technical solution design and troubleshooting.

  • 🎧 You are a great listener. You see your role as the voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our offerings continue to evolve in accordance with customer needs.

  • 📈 You are a problem solver. You thrive at solving complex challenges with innovative, scalable solutions.

  • ⚡️You know process matters. You are eager to improve processes and workflows to enhance efficiency and efficacy.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented and technically proficient. You take pride in internal operations.

  • 🤹You are adept at managing multiple simultaneous, multithreaded projects and have experience prioritizing based on customer and business needs.

  • 📊 You are data-driven. You use metrics and analytics to inform decisions and measure success.

  • 🌍 You are adaptable. You can navigate changes in a fast-paced, evolving environment, and would be happy to be the Workday SME in pre-sales conversations when needed.

  • 🧑‍🏫 You love to coach. You see every teaching moment as an opportunity and are excited to help our customers grow.

You might not be a great fit if:

  • You have limited experience leading Workday integrations.

  • You prefer an in-person role over remote.

  • You are less interested in customer-facing roles that require both technical and interpersonal skills.

jobs.title: Senior Paid Marketing Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hi 👋 I'm Harriet, and I lead Marketing at Ashby.

We've built a business with 5,500+ customers, a highly differentiated product, and a brand that people genuinely care about. We've invested in content, customer stories, community, and the foundations of a strong marketing program. Now, we have an opportunity to build a much bigger paid engine to support our next stage of growth.

We're looking for a Senior Paid Marketing Manager to build it.

You'll take ownership of our existing LinkedIn program and expand across Meta, Google Search, YouTube, and other channels. You'll have meaningful budget, strong creative and technical partners, and the autonomy to build a program that creates qualified pipeline and strengthens our brand.

This is a hands-on role. We want someone who knows their channels inside out, enjoys getting into the details, and can take a campaign from initial hypothesis through execution, analysis, and optimization. You'll have access to specialist support when it makes sense, but you'll be the person driving the work.

We also believe AI creates an opportunity for exceptional individual contributors to do work that previously required much larger teams. We're looking for someone who is already exploring that opportunity and wants to push it further.

What makes this role interesting

You get to build with the resources most marketers wish they had.

Paid is relatively underdeveloped at Ashby compared with the scale of our business. You get to build something substantial without unwinding years of accumulated complexity or fighting for the resources to make it work. We have strong content, customer proof, product differentiation, and an established brand. You'll start with a monthly budget in the hundreds of thousands of dollars and the support of our design, web, and RevOps teams.

You can rethink how paid marketing gets done.

We want to enable exceptional individual contributors to accomplish more through AI, automation, and better workflows. You'll have the freedom to experiment with new tools, build systems that improve your output, and challenge established ways of working.

You'll build a program that makes the brand and business stronger.

We believe great paid marketing combines analytical rigor with creative judgment. You'll optimize for pipeline and efficiency while building campaigns that earn attention, communicate our differentiation, and give the right buyers a reason to care about Ashby. We don't want a lead-generation machine that makes our brand worse.

What you'll own

Build and scale our paid program. Own strategy and execution across LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Search, expanding into YouTube and other channels as opportunities emerge. Prioritize audiences, develop campaign hypotheses, manage budgets, and turn promising experiments into repeatable sources of qualified pipeline.

Drive creative strategy and experimentation. Develop campaign concepts, write ad copy, brief creative, and shape landing-page tests. Work closely with design, content, and product marketing to produce distinctive work. Build a disciplined testing cadence across audiences, creative, offers, and conversion paths, knowing when to scale, iterate, or stop.

Use AI to increase your impact. Build practical workflows using AI, agents, and automation to improve research, creative iteration, campaign operations, and analysis. We want someone who actively experiments with new approaches, evaluates their effectiveness, and turns what works into repeatable systems.

Own measurement and performance. Drive our approach to paid measurement in partnership with RevOps. Establish the signals and reporting needed to understand qualified reach, conversion, pipeline contribution, and efficiency. Develop better ways to assess incrementality, make informed decisions with imperfect attribution, and translate performance data into clear investment recommendations.

Connect campaigns to the buyer journey. Partner with sales, lifecycle, and ABM to understand what makes an opportunity valuable and how paid can influence the journey from first touch through pipeline. Adapt messaging and investment to our customer segments and markets.

What you'll work on in your first six months

  • Take ownership of LinkedIn, identifying opportunities to improve qualified reach, creative, and progression into pipeline.

  • Build and scale Meta, establishing a strong creative testing cadence and the landing pages and follow-up needed to make the channel work.

  • Expand Google Search and launch YouTube, evaluating additional channels where there's a compelling audience and learning opportunity.

  • Establish a stronger operating system for paid, including AI-enabled workflows, measurement, and a clear approach to allocating investment.

The goal isn't to scale every channel equally. It's to build a broad set of opportunities, learn quickly, and concentrate investment where the evidence is strongest.

What we're looking for

We care more about what you've built and how you think than the number of years you've spent in marketing.

  • You're a domain expert in paid media. You have deep, hands-on expertise in LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Ads. You understand the platforms, know how to structure and optimize campaigns, and can explain how your decisions have influenced qualified pipeline. You've personally built and scaled programs in sales-led B2B SaaS.

  • You're a builder, not just a strategist. You're excited to get into the accounts, develop the creative, run experiments, investigate performance, and solve problems yourself. You know when external expertise can help, but you don't need an agency to do the core work.

  • You combine analytical rigor with creative taste. You understand performance metrics and experimentation, but you also know what makes advertising compelling. You can connect campaign decisions to buyer quality and pipeline without losing sight of the brand you're building.

  • You're already changing how you work with AI. You can demonstrate how you've used AI tools, agents, or automation to improve your output. You think critically about where automation helps, how to evaluate its results, and how to turn useful experiments into repeatable workflows.

  • You take ownership of measurement. You can work with CRM data, establish useful performance reporting, investigate attribution limitations, and drive better measurement approaches rather than waiting for someone else to provide the answers. You own budgeting and explain the case for reallocating investment.

  • You're a strong cross-functional partner. You work well with sales, design, content, product marketing, and RevOps. You seek out context, share what you learn, and care about the overall customer experience rather than optimizing your own channel in isolation.

Experience with YouTube, display, and programmatic is valuable, as is familiarity with HubSpot and measurement platforms like Dreamdata. You don't need to have mastered every channel, but you should have the expertise and judgment to expand beyond your core strengths.

This isn't the right role for you if

  • You prefer managing agencies to building campaigns. You want to set the strategy and have other people execute it, rather than getting into the details yourself.

  • You measure success primarily through platform metrics. You're satisfied with lower CPCs or more leads without understanding whether you're reaching the right buyers or contributing to pipeline.

  • You treat brand and performance as separate disciplines. You optimize individual campaigns without considering how the work shapes a prospect's perception of Ashby or contributes to long-term demand.

  • You haven't meaningfully changed how you work with AI. You're interested in the topic but haven't experimented with workflows, tools, or automation that improve your output.

  • You rely on other people to supply the ideas. You need a content team to hand you finished assets, a creative team to develop every concept, or an agency to tell you what to test next.

  • You prefer a proven playbook to an open-ended problem. You'd rather repeat an established formula than question assumptions, explore new opportunities, and work out what makes sense for this business.

  • You optimize your channel at the expense of the bigger picture. You don't enjoy collaborating with other teams or taking responsibility for the experience beyond the ad click.

We want someone who takes real pride in their craft, is generous with their expertise, and is excited to build something that the whole team can be proud of.

The tools you'll work with

Our core stack includes LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, HubSpot, and Dreamdata, alongside AI-assisted tools for research, creative development, analysis, and automation.

You'll also have access to design, web, and RevOps support, as well as specialist external partners when they can add meaningful value.

You don't need experience with every tool. You do need to be comfortable evaluating new ones, building useful workflows, and working independently with performance data.

A little about working at Ashby

We're building software that helps recruiting teams do some of their most important work better. We care deeply about the quality of our product, the experience we create for customers, and the company we're building along the way.

We value thoughtful, ambitious people who take ownership, communicate clearly, and keep improving. We give people meaningful responsibility and expect them to exercise good judgment in how they use it.

We're deliberate about how we work. We believe strong teams can accomplish a lot without unnecessary process, layers of management, or endless meetings. We make time for considered thinking, direct feedback, and the kind of collaboration that makes the work better.

If that sounds like an environment where you'd do your best work, we'd love to hear from you.

 

Interview Plan

Our interview process is:

  • 30 minutes intro call with Michelle (Recruiter Screen)

  • 45 minutes interview with Harriet (Hiring Manager)

  • 45 minutes interview with Sam (Paid Marketing Consultant)

  • Take-Home Assignment

    • Live Debrief to follow with Harriet and Sam

  • Final panel (1-1.5 hours)

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us and a 401k match.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

jobs.title: Director of Knowledge Management - NAMER
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hello!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Knowledge is one of the most important levers we have for delivering a great customer experience. Our knowledge ecosystem shapes how customers learn Ashby, how our Specialists resolve tickets, and how many customers never need to file a ticket at all. We have a tenured, talented Knowledge Management team doing excellent work. What we’re missing is someone to unify its work into a single, strategic practice.

That’s why we’re hiring our first Director of Knowledge Management. You’ll lead a team of Knowledge Managers and expand the team into new areas, including Digital Support experience and content localization.

You’ll set the vision, standards, and operating model that connect our customer-facing Help Center, internal Knowledge Base, and the self-service and in-app experiences built on them, including our AI Assistant. You’ll coach and develop a team that is growing and taking on new kinds of work, and you’ll be the voice of Knowledge in conversations with Support, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and beyond.

 

About the role

Today, our Knowledge Managers divide their work between internal and external content. You’ll help the team decide where to focus next, in what order, and how its structure should evolve to deliver on those priorities.

Knowledge Management is its own function at Ashby, separate from the internal and external enablement teams. You’ll build strong partnerships with both, defining clear boundaries and handoffs so content is consistent, never duplicated, and never left without an owner.

Your team will also co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, helping customers find the right knowledge when and where they need it. You’ll stay close enough to the content to coach with specifics, while relying on your team for the day-to-day execution of knowledge governance.

What you’ll own:

Set the Direction for Knowledge

  • Define the vision, roadmap, and success measures for Knowledge Management across internal and external content.

  • Identify the highest-impact opportunities to improve the knowledge ecosystem and sequence them against team capacity.

  • Build a clear model for content ownership, governance, and quality, streamlining how content is created, reviewed, and kept current as our product evolves.

  • Champion Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) practices and drive adoption across Support.

Lead and Develop the Team

  • Coach and develop Knowledge Managers through specific feedback on their work, clear career paths, and growth opportunities.

  • Evolve the team’s structure and divide work in the way that best serves customers and the business, with room to move beyond the current internal/external split.

  • Hire and onboard new team members next year, including Knowledge Managers, a Digital Support experience role, and a localization role.

Shape the AI Assistant’s Self-Service Experience

  • Co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, aligning on strategy, roadmap, and quality and partnering with Support, Support Operations, and Engineering on design and testing.

  • Help lead both declarative flows (structured, designed paths) and generative flows (AI-composed answers grounded in our content), and decide when each is the right tool.

  • Shape how content is structured, tagged, and governed so the Assistant surfaces accurate, current answers.

Build Our Localization Strategy

  • Build our localization strategy for Help Center content and drive the translation strategy for Customer Education, balancing quality, speed, and cost.

  • Define priorities for languages, content types, and tooling, and put processes in place to keep translated content in sync with the source.

Measure and Improve Results

  • Define and report on knowledge health, including content usage, search success, deflection, article quality, freshness, and the impact of knowledge on ticket volume and handle time. Treat deflection as a signal of customer success, not just cost reduction.

  • Measure how well the AI Assistant resolves customer questions, and use those conversations, ticket trends, customer feedback, and Specialist input to identify gaps and set content priorities.

Partner Across Ashby

  • Work closely with Customer Education and internal enablement in RevOps to align on ownership, standards, and a shared view of the customer and employee learning journey.

  • Partner with Product Marketing and Engineering so documentation keeps pace with releases and launches.

Requirements

  • Multiple years of experience leading knowledge management or content programs, setting strategy and building processes that scale with the business, ideally in B2B SaaS Support or Customer Experience.

  • Experience managing a team of content or knowledge professionals, including coaching people at different levels of experience.

  • Ability to connect knowledge across internal and external audiences, aligning Support, Product, Marketing, Engineering, and enablement teams around clear ownership and shared standards.

  • Experience designing or operating self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including both structured and generative flows, and a point of view on how knowledge quality shapes their performance.

  • Experience defining success measures for knowledge and using data to prioritize and make tradeoffs.

  • Comfort working in ambiguity as the function’s first dedicated leader, building on existing practices while setting a clear direction.

  • Strong writing and editing instincts. You’ll stay close enough to the work to set a high quality bar and give specific feedback.

  • Experience with KCS or comparable methodologies.

You should apply if:

  • You’ve led a knowledge management, documentation, or content program and managed a team of knowledge or content professionals.

  • You’ve designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including structured and generative flows, and understand how knowledge quality affects their performance.

  • You’re a strong writer and editor who can give specific feedback on the work, coach people at different levels, and help them grow.

  • You see knowledge as a strategic lever for customer experience and can bring teams together around clear ownership, shared standards, and measurable results.

  • You’re excited to build on an experienced team, shape how the function operates, and expand into new areas like Digital Support experience and localization.

 

You should not apply if:

  • Your background doesn’t include both managing a knowledge or content team and setting strategy for a knowledge, documentation, or content program.

  • You haven’t designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences.

  • You want a purely strategic role that keeps you removed from the content and the detailed feedback your team needs.

  • You need a fully built, fully staffed function or an established playbook to step into. We have a strong foundation, but several roles are still to be hired and the operating model is still taking shape.

  • You want sole ownership of AI product decisions or prefer to work only within a team you manage. This role depends on shared decisions with Product and strong partnerships across Ashby.

 

About Ashby

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com.

 

About Go To Market

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.

Interview process

Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical leadership, people management, communication, judgment, and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min

  • Hiring Manager interview — 45 min

  • Take-home assessment - 5 days to complete

  • Support Leadership — 45 min

  • Virtual Onsite — 75 min

    • Customer Self-Service Strategy — 30 min

    • Knowledge Team Leadership and Coaching — 30 min

    • Knowledge Strategy and Operating Model — 30 min

    • Closing Questions — 15 min

  • Founder interview — 30 min

 

Benefits

Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby—do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget.

  • A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop.

  • Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record)

  • Opportunities to spend time with teammates through an annual company offsite, team offsites, local meetups, and virtual events.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. jobs.title: Demo Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About this role

As Ashby’s first Demo Engineer, you’ll own the systems that make our demo environments reliable, current, and tailored — the infrastructure the entire go-to-market team leans on to show Ashby at its best. Today, AEs and SEs maintain and configure their own demo accounts by hand. That doesn’t scale: reps lose selling time, demos drift out of date, and every new product release widens the gap between what Ashby can do and what we can actually show live. Your job is to close that gap.

This is a net-new role. Right now, the work is split between ad hoc effort and a new set of disposable demo templates the Internal Platform team is building. You’ll own the layer on top of that foundation — customizing and extending those templates, generating realistic demo data, tailoring environments for specific verticals and new markets, and making sure every feature is demoable before it ships. You’ll sit within Solutions Engineering, reporting to the Global Head of Solutions Engineering, and partner closely with Internal Platform and Product teams.

Your work will be split roughly 70/30: about 70% owning, customizing, and extending the demo template system and the data and content inside it, and about 30% running demo readiness as a program — release readiness, documentation, and enablement so the GTM team always has current, credible demos to work with.

The best person for this job is genuinely hands-on technical — working with internal tools and configuration files, using APIs, and general data preparation — who gets energy from building leverage for a whole team rather than fixing one demo at a time.

You could be a great fit if:

  • 🛠 You’re comfortable working in JSON, calling REST / developer APIs, using AI tools, and scripting to configure and customize environments.

  • 🏗 You’re a builder, not just an operator. You get energy from creating systems and tooling that make a whole team more effective over time.

  • 🎥 You care deeply about demo quality. You understand what makes a product demo land, and you’re thoughtful about data realism and the narrative a demo needs to support.

  • 🧠 You have strong product intuition and can learn a deeply configurable product quickly, understanding how the different pieces connect.

  • 🔁 You have an iterative mindset. You like testing what works, refining over time, and improving based on what you learn from the field.

  • 🧩 You’re a systems thinker who would rather standardize and automate than manually repeat the same setup.

  • ⚡ You’re comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy a 0→1 role where the infrastructure is still being built around you.

  • 🤝 You partner well cross-functionally — with Engineering and with GTM — and can translate their needs into reliable systems.

  • 💙 You have empathy for the go-to-market teams you support and the Talent Acquisition space they sell into.

Bonus points for:

  • 📊 You’ve built demo environments, demo data, or sandbox/trial environments at a SaaS company before.

  • 🧰 You’ve written automation scripts or tooling to generate data or configure environments at scale.

  • 🎬 You’ve built and maintained a library of reusable, templated environments or assets that others relied on.

  • 🤝 You have experience with HR tech, ATS workflows, or recruiting operations.

Examples of things you’ll work on:

  • 🧱 Own the scaled demo system — customize and extend the demo environment infrastructure to support the GTM team.

  • 🗂 Generate realistic demo data — standardize and automate how demo environments are populated to eliminate manual setup.

  • 🎯 Build vertical- and market-specific demos — create tailored content for target verticals and additional languages as we move upmarket and expand internationally.

  • 🚦 Own demo readiness for new releases — make sure every feature is correctly configured and demoable in demo environments before it ships to GA.

  • 🧪 Stand up trial and sandbox environments — create templated environments prospects can use to test Ashby during the sales cycle.

  • 📚 Document how it all works — maintain clear documentation so the GTM team knows when and how to use each demo environment.

Why become a Demo Engineer at Ashby?

You’ll define a role that doesn’t exist yet. This is a net-new role designed around a real business need. You won’t inherit a mature playbook — you’ll build the infrastructure that lets the whole GTM team demo at a higher level.

Your work will compound. A great live demo helps one deal. A reliable, current, well-documented demo system improves every demo the entire go-to-market team runs. If you like creating leverage, this role has a lot of it.

The product gives you something real to work with. Ashby has strong product-market fit, and that matters here. You’re not manufacturing excitement around a weak product — you’re making it effortless to show something that already resonates when it’s shown well.

You’ll sit at the intersection of Engineering and GTM. This is a rare blend of technical building and understanding what the field actually needs. You’ll help translate our product releases into live deals — and connect the two.

The surface area keeps growing. As we ship new features and expand into new product areas, new verticals, and new geographies, demo needs compound with each release. There is a lot to build, and it only gets more interesting.

Reasons you shouldn’t apply:

  • If you want to be customer-facing or closing deals, this isn’t the right role — the impact here happens behind the scenes.

  • If you’re not genuinely hands-on technical — comfortable in JSON, APIs, and data — the core of this job will be frustrating.

  • If you need a fully built environment and a finished playbook, the ambiguity of a 0→1 role with infrastructure still being built will feel uncomfortable.

  • If continuously maintaining and updating environments as the product changes sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this won’t be a fit.

  • If you’d rather build production product features than internal tooling and demo systems, you’ll likely want a different engineering role.

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough — we want to make sure this role is the right fit for you and that you’re the right fit for Ashby. Details on the process for this role will be shared by your recruiter.

Benefits

  • You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

  • Sell a product that our customers are truly excited about.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby — do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

About Ashby

We’re building the next generation of recruiting software and we’re starting with a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run an efficient and data-driven hiring process.

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!).

We're in the talent acquisition software business. We run the end-to-end hiring process through our own platform, and ensure a level playing field for all candidates. Reaching out to hiring managers or recruiters directly won't improve your odds of success. Please focus your energy on the quality of your application.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Product Support Engineer - EMEA
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hello!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Product Support Engineer in EMEA 🎉

We’re expanding our global Support team to provide 24/7 coverage across time zones. You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in EMEA, with the ownership and visibility that come from being one of the first Support Engineers across European time zones. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process.

Not sure which Support role is right for you?

We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles.

  • Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

  • Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review.

About the role

Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As an early Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team.

What you’ll own

  • Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation—investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved.

  • Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues.

  • Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers.

  • Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement.

  • Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

  • Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence.

You should apply if:

  • You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior.

  • You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes.

  • You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones.

  • You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design.

  • You want to be an early technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team.

You should not apply if:

  • You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership.

  • Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deployment—and you haven’t worked extensively with customer-centric SaaS applications, APIs, logs, or data-backed troubleshooting.

  • You prefer to pass difficult issues to another team rather than reproduce, investigate, and explain them yourself.

  • You’re looking for a role focused mainly on writing production code; this role diagnoses and escalates bugs but does not own code changes.

  • You prefer clear-cut problems and predefined answers over working through ambiguity with careful documentation, focused questions, and evidence-based decisions.

  • You want a narrowly defined role without regional operating ownership or projects that improve how the broader Support team works.

About Ashby

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com.

About Go To Market

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.

Interview process

Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical reasoning, communication precision, and ownership.

  • Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min

  • Take-home assessment — 5 days to complete

  • Hiring Manager interview — 45–60 min

  • Virtual onsite — 120 min

    • Meet the team — 30 min

    • Technical & integration skills — 45 min

    • CS and Support leadership — 30 min

    • Closing questions — 15 min

Onboarding

Your onboarding will combine Ashby-wide product and company training with a Support Engineering-specific ramp plan. You’ll learn the product and support workflow, get familiar with the tools and systems used for technical investigations, and build relationships across Support, Product, and Engineering. With support from your manager and onboarding buddy, you’ll take on increasingly complex investigations as you build context, with regular check-ins throughout your first 90 days.

Benefits

Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget.

  • A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop.

  • Opportunities to spend time with teammates through an annual company offsite, team offsites, local meetups, and virtual events.

  • Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record)

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Manager, Technical Services
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Manager of Technical Services

Hi, I’m John and I’m the Head of Professional Services at Ashby. One of my favorite aspects of Ashby is our operating principle of Continuous Improvement. Coupled with our principle of caring deeply about our customers, we often find ourselves wondering ‘what is a better way to accomplish this’. That’s why I am thrilled to be hiring our first Technical Services Manager! As a leader on our growing Professional Services team (within Ashby’s Customer Success organization), you’ll have the opportunity to play a key role early in our customers’ journey, ultimately up-leveling the overall customer experience.

The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we now support thousands of customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. As we scale upmarket, we are increasingly partnering with larger, highly complex organizations that bring sophisticated HR tech stacks requiring more customized integrations. To meet this demand, our technical services function is expanding quickly, and we are looking for our first dedicated leader to guide this talented group of individual contributors through our next phase of scale. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role.

The Role:

We’re looking for our first Manager of Technical Services to be the strategic anchor for Ashby’s expanding technical integration services. This role bridges two distinct technical engines: you will oversee specialized integration consultants dedicated to deep Workday integrations, as well as a team of technical solution consultants who build bespoke API solutions, craft custom recommendations, and deliver hands-on technical builds for our customers.

Six months in, success looks like having a highly efficient, scaled team that seamlessly handles multiple concurrent complex integrations, successfully troubleshoots mid-flight technical challenges, and consistently delivers high-value technical consulting. The impact you will have is substantial; you will help shape our technical services strategy and ensure all customers can cohesively integrate Ashby into their complex HR tech stacks.

You will achieve this by:

  • Building and scaling a high-performing team, supporting both specialized Integration Consultants and Technical Solution Consultants; empowering them to comfortably manage high-volume portfolios while maintaining Ashby's high standards for quality.

  • Building the operational infrastructure required to scale technical services, including capacity planning, project prioritization, quality standards, and repeatable delivery processes. You know when to standardize, when to customize, and how to balance speed, quality, and customer outcomes.

  • Acting as a senior escalation point, leveraging your foundational knowledge of Workday architecture and complex API capabilities to guide your team. Diving into active integrations, troubleshooting roadblocks, and translating ambiguity into clear technical paths, helping your team scope solutions.

  • Owning the evolution of our technical services offerings, identifying recurring customer needs, evaluating opportunities to standardize solutions, and determining where new technical capabilities will deliver the greatest customer and business impact.

  • Partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Implementation to distinguish product gaps from services opportunities, establish clear ownership of complex technical challenges, and ensure customer commitments are both technically feasible and commercially sound.

As you're probably gathering, we're looking for someone who has been in the trenches, led high-volume functions, and built and scaled a team of technical consultants. You've done this work yourself, and you bring real "I've been there" credibility and empathy for customers navigating complex tools.

To be qualified for this role, you must have the following:

  • 8+ years of experience in technical consulting, integration services, or technical implementations, with at least 3+ years directly managing and scaling a team of technical resources.

  • Strong working knowledge of enterprise integrations, including Workday architecture, APIs, authentication, data mapping, and integration design. You can critically evaluate proposed solutions, identify technical risks, and guide consultants through complex implementation challenges, ultimately translating these concepts into clear, actionable strategies for non-technical audiences and executive stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated success guiding a team of consultants through a high-volume portfolio of mid-to-large tier enterprise organizations. You know how to orchestrate moving pieces, keep a mixed-discipline team on track, and balance bandwidth across concurrent enterprise projects.

  • Experience actively building a team by anticipating future gaps, looking around the corner to determine what technical capabilities or services we will need next before the demand even hits.

If you need someone else to do any of the following, then this role is probably not for you:

  • Dive into the technical details; if you prefer to manage from a distance rather than understand the underlying architecture and challenge technical decisions, this isn't a fit.

  • Brainstorm and validate solutions to complex integration hurdles when your team gets stuck.

  • Scope mid-flight pivots; when a customer suddenly requires a custom build instead of a standard integration, you must be able to step in and define that technical path.

  • Manage the reality of scale; if you are only comfortable overseeing singular, monolithic deployments rather than a high-volume portfolio of concurrent projects across your team.

Instructions

Please take your time with your application and the application questions. Although we use AI to assist in our review, we never use AI to auto-qualify or disqualify candidates. We lay eyes on each and every application, and speak to a very select group of candidates based on the application as a whole.

 
 

The Interview

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

  • 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Talent Team

  • 45 min - Interview with the Head of Professional Services

  • 60 min- Mock Call with an Integrations Consultant and Product Manager

  • Final Round:

    • 30 min - Cross-Functional Interview with a CS Leader

    • 30 min - Leadership Interview with VP of Customer Success

    • 30 min - Interview with the CEO

    • 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager

Our Philosophy

Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

  • We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly.

  • We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Operating Principles to get a sense of what we are looking for in folks on the team.

 

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with 100% of premiums covered by us.

  • 401(k) with a 3% employer contribution.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Head of Global Support
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hi I’m Kelsey 👋 – VP of CS at Ashby. One of my favorite Ashby principles is Implementing Continuous Improvement; it guides how we continually raise the bar on the customer experience. I’m thrilled to be hiring a Head of Global Support to lead our global team and take our world-class support to the next level.

Our product and growth are exceptional. Ashby’s All-in-One solution is powerful, easy to use, and often replaces 4-5 disparate solutions (ATS, scheduling, analytics, sourcing and CRM). We have several thousand customers, including notable organizations like Shopify and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we’re growing >100% year over year, with very low churn and healthy expansion.

About this role:

As our Head of Global Support, you’ll lead an exceptional team of (2) Heads of, (5) Managers, and (~60) highly technical individual contributors dedicated to delivering remarkable support across every customer segment – from early-stage startups to strategic enterprise organizations. Over the next year, you’ll nearly double this team.

You’ll define how Ashby scales Support as our customer base and product suite grow, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success leadership. Our industry-leading G2 rating reflects our unrelenting high bar: “users rave about Ashby’s top-notch support, noting quick responses and a thoughtful, user-focused approach.”

You’ll build on that foundation: driving continuous improvement, advancing automation, and evolving our 24/7 support model.

Role requirements:

  • Customer-Centric Platform Experience: You lead an exceptional global support function for a complex suite of B2B SaaS products, delivering a measurable best-in-class experience.

  • Leadership: You have a proven track record of successfully leading and scaling high-performing SaaS Customer Support Teams (we raised our Series D last year and are poised for continued growth).

  • Strategic & Operational: You demonstrate a strong command of support operations, including SLAs, schedule optimization, and queue management. You’re experienced in designing efficient support models (ideally including 24/7 coverage, escalation workflows, and specialization). You know how to move resolution up-funnel.

  • Cross-functional Partnership: You collaborate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders across Customer Success, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Operations to align support insights with roadmap and customer outcomes.

  • Data-Driven, Innovative, and Operational: You leverage data and technology to improve efficiency and quality; comfortable using metrics (CSAT, response times, self-service rates) to inform decisions. You view metrics as a window into the customer experience, not just operational goals, and translate insights into actions that elevate their experience. You proactively address thematic customer issues and improve Support processes to enhance both the efficiency and efficacy of the Support Team.

  • Training and Development: You are excited to further our training programs with the goal of empowering our team with the skills and knowledge required to excel in the Support function.

You could be a great fit if:

  • 🧠 You are high ceiling. We’re prioritizing high trajectory, principled thinkers over folks who are resting on ‘seen it, done it’.

  • 📣 You communicate with clarity. You ask precise questions and can distill complex concepts into simple themes.

  • 🎧 You are a great listener. You see your role as 1) advocate for the Support Team as well as 2) voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our product roadmap continues to move our work forward.

  • 📈 You are a strategic problem solver. You thrive at solving complex challenges with principled, scalable solutions.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You take pride in internal operations.

  • ⚡️You are process-oriented – not for bureaucracy’s sake, but because great systems free people to do their best work.

  • ⭐ You stay close to the product. You believe that truly exceptional support comes from deep product understanding – and that everyone on the team shares responsibility for knowing, using, and championing the product we build.

This role may not be a great fit if:

  • You don’t need to have already run a massive, multi-layered Support organization; but you do need to show a track record of growing scope, complexity, and ownership. This might look like starting with front-line Support and progressively taking on escalations, incident management, cross-functional problem solving, or operational leadership. We’re looking for someone with the judgment and ambition to scale a full-fledged Support organization over time, and to instill a culture of end-to-end accountability for customer outcomes.

  • You’re accustomed to supporting a point solution or simple product. Ashby is sufficiently robust (and increasingly so as we become a platform solution); our Support leader must be familiar with supporting complex products.

  • You prefer to focus solely on strategic priorities. We expect that even our most senior leaders are able to ‘traverse the elevation’ and be in the particulars as necessary.

Our Philosophy

Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

  • We offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • You can learn more here about our philosophy.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using optimal communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process.

The Interview

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

  • 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Senior Recruiter

  • 45-60 min - Interview with VP of CS (Hiring Manager)

  • 45-60 min - Interview with Head of Support

  • Final Round:

    • 60 min - Practical Exercise with Support Leaders

    • 30 min - Interview with Head of CS

    • 30 min - Interview with CEO

    • 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager

Benefits

  • You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

  • Competitive compensation is offered.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.
